 Lakers News JJ Redick wants to try Lakers lineups with Luka and Austin both on bench
 Last updated: November 19, 2026 2:12 pm 
 Lakers Daily 
 Share 
 7 Min Read 
 IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect 
 JJ Redick wants to see what the Los Angeles Lakers can get out of a lineup with Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves resting at the same time. One reason has as much to do with who will play alongside them in the fourth quarter as it does with who can run the offense while they sit.
 Asked before Wednesday’s game against the Utah Jazz whether Quentin Grimes had earned a permanent starting spot, Redick said the coaching staff had been discussing a different way to get its other guards involved. Once the Lakers are healthy, he wants to give those players a stretch to generate offense on their own.
 By the time he has to pick five players to finish a close game, he’d like to have more options who have already found their shot. Redick described the lineup he wants to try as one with “no Luka, no AR.”
 The Lakers had yet to get the run of games together that he wanted to give it a fair look. But they had just played five minutes against the Charlotte Hornets that offered a pretty good illustration of what he meant.
 Quentin Grimes got going before Luka Doncic checked back in
 Grimes’ 10th 3-pointer against Charlotte was the one that forced overtime. His first three of the fourth quarter are worth another look.
 Reaves was out, Doncic was on the bench and the Hornets had stretched their lead to 14 with 11 minutes left. The Lakers had Grimes and Collin Sexton out there with Ziaire Williams, Carson Cooper and Sandro Mamukelashvili to open the period.
 The first two baskets that group produced after falling behind 97-83 were dunks. Grimes found a cutting Mamukelashvili for the first one.
 On the next Lakers possession, Grimes made the cut himself and Sexton delivered the pass. Less than a minute and a half later, Grimes had added a pair of 3s, with a steal in between. Three different Lakers had already assisted on his baskets.
 At the 7:48 mark, Sexton found Grimes for another 3 from 29 feet. That cut the deficit to six. When Doncic came back with 6:54 remaining, Grimes was at the line shooting two free throws.
 He made the second to bring Los Angeles within four. Redick had gotten more than five minutes of rest for Doncic to start the quarter, and the Lakers had played their way back into a game they had trailed by double digits.
 What happened after the substitution might be more important for Grimes’ chances of finishing games. Redick said after the win that once Doncic recognized how well Grimes was shooting, he started waving off plays his coach called so he could get his teammate the ball.
 With Charlotte up four in the final minute, Doncic set up Grimes for a layup. After a Hornets free throw, he found him again for the 3 that tied it at 111. Grimes scored 21 of his career-high 47 points in the fourth.
 QUENTIN GRIMES SENDS IT TO OT pic.twitter.com/w0ARZykZ6g 
 — Lakers Daily (@LakersDailyCom) November 18, 2026 
 Redick kept both Grimes and Sexton with Doncic to start overtime. When a Naz Reid 3 put Charlotte ahead, Sexton brought the Lakers within one at the line.
 Doncic then hit the short jumper that gave Los Angeles the lead. All three guards had a hand in the 118-114 win.
 Redick recalled Doncic changing those plays on Tuesday night. Sexton offered another detail about the scorer they were looking for.
 In the days leading up to the game, he said, Grimes had sometimes seemed caught between taking a shot and passing it up. His teammates had been urging him to trust the first decision.
 “We believe in you. We know how good you are,” Sexton said .
 What changes for Grimes when Austin Reaves returns?
 Playing alongside Doncic and Reaves gives Grimes a different job. Redick said Grimes is comfortable catching and shooting off the two guards.
 The question for the coaching staff is how to preserve some of the freedom he had against Charlotte when two of the Lakers’ best options to create a shot are back on the floor together. Grimes scored another 20 points Wednesday in a 109-97 loss to Utah.
 Afterward, he was asked about his conversations with Redick and how they could keep him involved whether he started or came off the bench. Grimes called it “a good problem to have.”
 He said he welcomed having a coach who wanted to put the ball in his hands and expected Redick to keep finding opportunities for him once the team got healthy.
 There’s still a distinction between what worked Tuesday and what Redick wants to find out. Grimes had already played three quarters as a starter when he took the floor alongside Sexton to open the fourth.
 Could a player coming off the bench get comfortable enough in a shorter stretch to give Redick the same choice late? And if Grimes got hot with the second unit, how long would Redick keep him out there once both starting guards were ready to return?
 Redick left the starting job open. Injuries and rest would give several players turns with the first group over a long season, he said. Reaves’ bruised left heel had already given Grimes an opportunity to show how much scoring he could take on.
 The more interesting substitution when Reaves is back could come well after tipoff. If Redick sends Grimes and Sexton out together while both starters sit, watch who stays on the floor when Doncic and Reaves head back to the scorer’s table.
